source.title: Behavioral Compositionality of Sparse Autoencoder Representations
source.authors: Hao-Tian Ma; Zi-Ye Mei; Frederic Sala

record.file_problem: Full text is present. Some mathematical notation and table formatting are flattened, but the reported results are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests behavioral compositionality of selected SAE contributions, not superposition geometry, neuron polysemanticity, feature sparsity/importance effects, or the canonicality of SAE features as specified by the claim versions. Its results are related to feature interactions but do not test a listed version.
record.gate_note: The paper reports many results on behavioral residuals, coordinate rotations, pairwise fits, steering, and depth. These measure downstream compositionality of selected SAE contributions, not overlapping near-orthogonal feature directions or the other listed claim versions. The adjacent compositionality results are recorded under fits_no_version. The affine controls and other protocol checks are not rows about the claim.
record.test_reason: The study takes SAE features (the dictionary-learning product behind V4/V5) as given objects. It measures whether their downstream behavioral effects compose additively, using a new SAR metric. It does not measure superposition geometry, neuron polysemanticity, capacity or sparsity effects, dictionary completeness, stability or canonicality, or feature dimensionality. The rotation comparison shows learned SAE coordinates are more first-order compositional than random sum-preserving rotations. That is a privileged-basis-style result about behavioral additivity, not a test of whether SAE features are complete, stable, canonical units (V5). The authors state their conclusions are not a global property of an SAE dictionary. All results therefore fall outside the listed versions, and the record's fits_no_version entries are appropriate. The reader's 'discusses/T6' undersells that SAEs are used as the working tool; 'uses_without_test/T4' fits better.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. Authors conclude SAE coordinates support comparatively compositional behavioral descriptions (lower SAR1 than rotations), but are not fully additive: pairwise terms improve joint prediction and steering prediction. SAR differs from reconstruction quality, and conclusions depend on selected contributions, readout, and intervention distribution.
record.recipe_differences: The study develops and evaluates a behavioral compositionality measurement for SAE coordinates; it does not reproduce the superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported behavioral residuals and related measures vary with behavior, representation layer, coordinate system, selected feature count, and intervention magnitude. The paper reports lower SAR with milder interventions and depth-dependent results.

fits_no_version.finding: Learned SAE coordinates had lower first-order behavioral residual (SAR1) than sum-preserving random rotations of the same selected subspace in all 18 fixed-layer settings and all 33 model-behavior-layer comparisons. The gap was marginal in Gemma IOI and Mistral greater-than.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under subset interventions, learned SAE coordinates give a more first-order-compositional behavioral description than random rotations of the same subspace (a behavioral privileged-basis property).

fits_no_version.finding: Pairwise terms improved held-out rank fidelity and reduced ordering error in all 18 settings. They also beat parameter-matched random third-order models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Effects of co-active SAE features on downstream behavior are not additive; pairwise interactions carry substantial structure.

fits_no_version.finding: For combinations of 16 published steering directions, pairwise modeling improved overall MMLU-Pro prediction. Domain results were heterogeneous.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Combined SAE steering effects require interaction terms to predict.

record.problems: The measured outcomes are behavioral coalition predictions, not measurements of feature-direction geometry or neuron polysemanticity. The authors note that the fitted second-order residual is not a high-precision estimate of its population value; residual magnitudes vary with coalition sampling, and the study's conclusions are limited to selected contributions, readouts, and intervention distributions.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted other adjacent compositionality results, including sign error and selection regret, depth profiles, reconstruction-quality comparisons, the matched random third-order control, additional model pipelines, and per-domain steering results. The retained rows prioritize the fixed-layer coordinate comparison, the 18 fixed-layer pairwise comparisons, and the overall steering result; these omitted outcomes are in sections 4.3–4.7 and Appendices G–I.

untested.parts: No toy models; no sparsity-dependent geometry or near-orthogonal overlapping directions measured.
No neuron-level polysemanticity or capacity/importance allocation measured.
No analysis of polysemanticity arising without capacity pressure.
Does not test whether features spread across neurons or whether SAEs recover sparse features. SAEs are used as given.
Completeness, stability across runs, and canonicality of SAE features not measured. The rotation and six-SAE comparisons concern behavioral additivity, not canonicality.
Multidimensional features only cited in related work (Engels et al.); not tested.

record.verdict_notes: No result bears on superposition per se. The six-SAE Gemma-3 1B comparison (SAR varies across dictionary size and L0) could loosely relate to V5's stability or canonicality. However, it measures behavioral additivity, not feature identity, so it is not a V5 test. Rows are accurately transcribed from Tables 1, 10, 17 and 18.

versions.untested_parts: Whether sparse features outnumber dimensions, are represented by overlapping near-orthogonal directions, or show sparsity-dependent geometric transitions.
Whether neuron polysemanticity arises from capacity competition, and whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemanticity occurs without capacity pressure.
Whether features spread across neurons or whether SAEs recover sparse features as described in the version.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, canonical units of model representation.
Whether represented features are one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

relation.reason: SAE features are inputs to the analysis; downstream interaction and ordering measurements do not test the catalog's superposition claims.

tranche.reason: Uses existing SAE coordinates and steering directions to evaluate behavioral compositionality and prediction methods; does not test V1–V6.

source_check.notes: The authors-conclusion paraphrase is accurate. Domain rank fidelity declines in Economics, Engineering, Law and Math; the aggregate improvement does not establish superposition.
